internationalism.description: Advocacy of greater political or economic cooperation among nations and peoples.

federation.description: A political entity characterized by a union of partially self-governing states or regions under a central government.

communal.description: Relating to religious or ethnic communities, often used in the context of communal electorates or tensions.

dacoities.description: Armed robberies or banditry, especially in rural India.

reactionary.description: Opposing political or social progress or reform.

obscurantist.description: Deliberately preventing the facts or full details of something from becoming known.

autocratic.description: Relating to a ruler who has absolute power.

executive orders.description: Directives issued by an authority, such as a governor, with the force of law.

statutory.description: Required, permitted, or enacted by statute (law).

mercenaries.description: Soldiers hired to serve in a foreign army.

feudal.description: Relating to the social system in medieval Europe or similar hierarchical systems.

autocratic ruler.description: A ruler with absolute power over a state or people.

residuary powers.description: Powers retained by the constituent units of a federation that are not delegated to the central government.

collaborators.description: People who cooperate traitorously with an enemy occupying their country.

home guards.description: Civilian volunteer forces organized for local defense.

guerrilla.description: Member of a small independent group taking part in irregular fighting, typically against larger regular forces.

bullock-cart.description: Traditional Indian vehicle drawn by oxen, used for rural transport.

H.J. Mackinder.description: British geographer and geopolitical theorist, known for his 'heartland' theory.

George Bernard Shaw.description: Renowned British playwright and critic who commented on the British Empire, Churchill, and Gandhi.

Thucydides.description: Ancient Greek historian, cited for his analysis of empire and democracy.

Plato.description: Ancient Greek philosopher, referenced for his views on the unity of body and soul.

Lao Tzu.description: Ancient Chinese philosopher, quoted for his reflections on life and passion.

Aristotle.description: Ancient Greek philosopher, cited for his thoughts on human perfection and immortality.

Nicolai Ostrovsky.description: Soviet writer, quoted for his views on life and the purpose of human existence.

Indonesia.description: A Southeast Asian country, referenced in the context of anti-colonial struggles.

acquisitive.description: Characterized by a strong desire to acquire and possess things, especially material wealth.
